evidence.quote:
A brief discussion on why previous reviews failed to consider adverse effects
would also be beneficial. Is it possible that primary research included in these systematic reviews
overlooked these factors?

I am not sure I understand this comment. It is common practice to extract these from SRs in
a systematic review of reviews (OoO). We do not contend that previous SRs have failed to
consider these factors, but rather are adhering to best practice in a systematic review of
reviews. Risk of bias is unlikely to have been assessed by the primary study, subgroup
effects may also not be reported in all studies, but may have only been possible to calculate
in a SR. It is not always clear whether primary studies report adverse effects, and any
discussion of why previous reviews failed to consider adverse effects would be speculation,
as we have no clues as to why.
